problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of a differentiable convex function f:E→ℝ with globally L-Lipschitz gradient, L>0. A global minimizer x⋆ exists with ‖x0−x⋆‖≤R, R≥0; strong convexity is not required.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Each query x returns g(x,Zk) along one stationary, exogenous Markov trajectory. For every fixed x, ∫g(x,z)π(dz)=∇f(x). Conditional unbiasedness at adaptive queries is not assumed. Replies contain only gradient vectors; every oracle call advances the trajectory index.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HeavyTailedMarkovSmoothAndConvex.lean: pathLaw and spec.admissible oracle equality and stationary-gradient identity; LongTails/Template.lean: execute and _run.

distinctive_assumptions.label: markov_dependence
distinctive_assumptions.details: Z0∼π and κπ=π. For every integer t≥0, ∫sup_{A measurable}|κ^t(z,A)−π(A)|π(dz)≤(1+t/τ)^−β, where τ>0 and β>0. This is stationary-average polynomial total-variation mixing, without a uniform-over-states mixing assumption.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HeavyTailedMarkovSmoothAndConvex.lean: mixingDistance, pathLaw, and spec.admissible invariance and mixing inequality.

distinctive_assumptions.label: heavy_tailed_noise
distinctive_assumptions.details: For all x, ∫‖g(x,z)−∇f(x)‖^α π(dz)≤σ^α, with σ≥0 and 1<α≤2. The central moment bound is stationary and uniform in x; for α<2, finite variance is not required.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HeavyTailedMarkovSmoothAndConvex.lean: spec.valid and spec.admissible central-moment integrability and inequality.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a complete, second-countable real Hilbert space with its Borel measurable structure; finite dimensionality is not required. All Params, including L,R,σ,α,τ,β,ε and x0, are public. The objective f and oracle witnesses g,κ,π are hidden. Algorithms may randomize independently of the oracle and must use a fixed oracle-call budget.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HeavyTailedMarkovSmoothAndConvex.lean: Params, spec.Public, spec.publicInput, and spec.admissible existential witnesses; LongTails/Template.lean: Algorithm and Convergence.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: Return a measurable E-valued output X with integrable objective gap f(X)−f(x⋆) for some global minimizer x⋆. No particular iterate or averaging rule is prescribed.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: E[f(X)−f(x⋆)]≤ε, ε>0, under the joint product law of algorithm randomness and the stationary Markov oracle trajectory.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HeavyTailedMarkovSmoothAndConvex.lean: spec.successful and spec.valid; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence product probability law.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: Smooth convex optimization is classical, but this formulation combines stationary finite-α-moment gradient noise with stationary-average polynomial Markov mixing in a potentially infinite-dimensional Hilbert space.

descriptionHtml:
Convex Minimization with Markov Noise

We consider minimizing a differentiable convex function f:E→R on a separable real Hilbert space E. Its gradient is L-Lipschitz, where L>0, and a given point x0∈E is within distance R≥0 of a global minimizer x⋆. At query x, the oracle returns g(x,Zk), where (Zk)k≥0 is a stationary, polynomially mixing Markov chain. Under its stationary law, g is unbiased and its centered α-moment is at most σα, with 1<α≤2 and σ≥0. For ε>0, the goal is a measurable output x¯ with integrable objective gap and E[f(x¯)−f(x⋆)]≤ε, averaging over oracle and independent algorithm randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈Ef(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product on E. Let Ω be a measurable sample space, and let τ>0 and β>0 be the mixing parameters. The algorithm receives E, Ω, L, R, σ, α, τ, β, ε, and x0; the objective and the oracle’s sampling law are accessed through oracle replies.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Convexity and smoothness). The function f is Fréchet differentiable everywhere on E. For every x,y∈E and s∈[0,1], f((1−s)x+sy)≤(1−s)f(x)+sf(y),∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥.

Assumption 2 (Initial distance). There exists x⋆∈E such that f(x⋆)≤f(x)for every x∈E,∥x0−x⋆∥≤R.

Assumption 3 (Stationary Markov sampling and mixing). The samples form a time-homogeneous Markov chain on Ω with transition probability kernel κ and initial distribution π, where π is a probability measure. It is invariant: for every measurable A⊆Ω, EZ∼π[κ(Z,A)]=π(A). For each integer t≥0, define the total-variation distance using the convention dt(z)=supA⊆Ωmeasurable|κt(z,A)−π(A)|, where κt is the t-step transition kernel and κ0(z,⋅) is the point mass at z. The function dt is integrable under π and satisfies EZ∼π[dt(Z)]≤(1+tτ)−β,t=0,1,2,….

Assumption 4 (Stationary oracle moments). The map g:E×Ω→E is jointly measurable. For every fixed x∈E, g(x,⋅) is Bochner integrable under π, the function ∥g(x,⋅)−∇f(x)∥α is integrable under π, and EZ∼π[g(x,Z)]=∇f(x),EZ∼π[∥g(x,Z)−∇f(x)∥α]≤σα. These moment conditions are taken under the stationary law at each fixed query point.

Queries may be made at any point of E. The oracle returns g(xk,Zk) on call k, starting at k=0 and using consecutive states of the same chain. The query xk may depend on previous replies and on algorithm randomness, which is independent of the chain. Any calls whose replies are discarded still count toward the oracle-call budget.

After the allotted calls, the output x¯∈E must be measurable, its objective gap must be integrable, and it must satisfy EP[f(x¯)−f(x⋆)]≤ε, where P is the joint law of the Markov chain and the independent algorithm randomness.

comparisonHtml:
On a second-countable real Hilbert space with its Borel measurable structure, f is convex and differentiable with L-Lipschitz gradient and a minimizer x⋆ satisfying ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R. The jointly measurable oracle satisfies ∫g(x,z)dπ(z)=∇f(x) and ∫∥g(x,z)−∇f(x)∥αdπ(z)≤σα, with the corresponding integrability assumptions. Samples follow a stationary Markov chain with kernel κ, invariant probability π, and integrable dt(z)=TV(κt(z,⋅),π) satisfying ∫dtdπ≤(1+t/τ)−β for every lag. Here L,τ,β,ε>0, R,σ≥0, and 1<α≤2. Target: measurable output with integrable gap and ∫[f(output(ω))−f(x⋆)]dP(ω)≤ε, where P is the stationary path law.

On the geometric overlap, pays τmix on the deterministic term, up to logarithms; noise order matches up to logarithms.
(3) Ergodic mirror descent (Duchi et al. 2012), Thm. 1, (12); derived bound O(1+Q2[1+τQ1/β]) calls, fixed β. Special case: finite-dimensional ball; convex sample losses with ∥g∥≤G; uniform dt≤(1+t/τ)−β. (1): Scope: no bounded-gradient requirement; averaged rather than uniform mixing. Output: last accelerated iterate instead of averaging. (1): Needs smoothness and stationary start. For α=2, σ≍G, A≤Q2, Q→∞, fixed τ,β: O(τQ2+2/β) versus O(τQ2+1/β).
(4) Accelerated stochastic proximal subgradient (He et al. 2026), Thm. 2(i), (7a) O(1+A+(σR/ε)α/(α−1)) calls, fixed α. Special case: i.i.d., finite-dimensional ball, h=ιB(x0,R), 0<ε<1. (1): Scope: stationary Markov dependence. Matches known i.i.d. rate when τ permits skip length m=1, for fixed α. (1): Requires clipping; (4) does not.

Fixed-exponent bounds need not have uniform constants as α↓1 or β↓0. ι denotes a convex-set indicator.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function
import Mathlib.Probability.Kernel.IonescuTulcea.Traj
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pow.Real

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.HeavyTailedMarkovSmoothAndConvex

open OracleTemplate

noncomputable def pathLaw {Ω : Type} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
    (κ : Kernel Ω Ω) [IsMarkovKernel κ] (initial : ProbabilityMeasure Ω) :
    ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → Ω) :=
  ⟨Kernel.trajMeasure (initial : Measure Ω)
    (fun n => κ.comap (fun z : Finset.Iic n → Ω => z ⟨n, Finset.mem_Iic.mpr le_rfl⟩)
      (by fun_prop)), inferInstance⟩

noncomputable def mixingDistance {Ω : Type} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
    (κ : Kernel Ω Ω) (π : ProbabilityMeasure Ω) (t : ℕ) (z : Ω) : ℝ :=
  ⨆ s : {s : Set Ω // MeasurableSet s},
    |((κ ^ t) z s.val).toReal - ((π : Measure Ω) s.val).toReal|

structure Params where
  E : Type u
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [completeE : CompleteSpace E]
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  [borelE : BorelSpace E]
  [countableE : SecondCountableTopology E]
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  L : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  σ : ℝ
  α : ℝ
  τ : ℝ
  β : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Params.normedE Params.linearE Params.completeE Params.measurableE Params.borelE Params.countableE Params.measurableΩ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := p.E → ℝ
  Query p := p.E
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput p := p
  valid q :=
    0 < q.L ∧ 0 ≤ q.R ∧ 0 ≤ q.σ ∧ 1 < q.α ∧ q.α ≤ 2 ∧ 0 < q.τ ∧ 0 < q.β ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q f O :=
    ∃ (g : q.E → q.Ω → q.E) (κ : Kernel q.Ω q.Ω) (hκ : IsMarkovKernel κ)
        (π : ProbabilityMeasure q.Ω),
      O = { Seed := fun _ => q.Ω
            law := @pathLaw q.Ω _ κ hκ π
            answer := fun _ (_, x) z => g x z } ∧
      κ ∘ₘ (π : Measure q.Ω) = (π : Measure q.Ω) ∧
      (∀ t, Integrable (mixingDistance κ π t) (π : Measure q.Ω)) ∧
      (∀ t, (∫ z, mixingDistance κ π t z ∂(π : Measure q.Ω)) ≤
        (1 + (t : ℝ) / q.τ) ^ (-q.β)) ∧
      ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ f ∧
      (∀ x, HasGradientAt f (gradient f x) x) ∧
      (∀ x y, ‖gradient f x - gradient f y‖ ≤ q.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
      (∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧ ‖q.x0 - xstar‖ ≤ q.R) ∧
      Measurable (Function.uncurry g) ∧
      (∀ x, Integrable (g x) (π : Measure q.Ω)) ∧
      (∀ x, ∫ z, g x z ∂(π : Measure q.Ω) = gradient f x) ∧
      (∀ x, Integrable (fun z => ‖g x z - gradient f x‖ ^ q.α) (π : Measure q.Ω)) ∧
      (∀ x, (∫ z, ‖g x z - gradient f x‖ ^ q.α ∂(π : Measure q.Ω)) ≤ q.σ ^ q.α)
  successful q f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
    ∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧
      Integrable (fun ω => f (output ω) - f xstar) (P : Measure _) ∧
      (∫ ω, f (output ω) - f xstar ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.HeavyTailedMarkovSmoothAndConvex
